We propose a categorical description for these TDLs, dubbed as ``para-fusion category", which contains various novel features, including $\mathbb Z_M$ $q$-type objects for $M\vert N$, and parafermoinic defect operators as a type of specialized 1-morphisms of the TDLs. The para-fusion category in parafermionic CFTs can be regarded as a natural generalization of the super-fusion category for the description of TDLs in 2d fermionic CFTs. We investigate these distinguishing features in para-fusion category from both a 2d pure CFT perspective, and also a 3d anyon condensation viewpoint. In the latter approach, we introduce a generalized parafermionic anyon condensation, and use it to establish a functor from the parent fusion category for TDLs in bosonic CFTs to the para-fusion category for TDLs in the parafermionized ones. At last, we provide many examples to illustrate the properties of the proposed para-fusion category, and also give a full classification for a universal para-fusion category obtained from parafermionic condensation of Tambara-Yamagami $\mathbb Z_N$ fusion category.
item.dc:creator: Jin Chen, Babak Haghighat, Qing-Rui Wang

item.title: Asymmetry Amplification by a Nonadiabatic Passage through a Critical Point
item.description: arXiv:2408.15897v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose and solve a minimal model of dynamic passage through a second-order phase transition in the presence of symmetry breaking interactions and no dissipation. Our model generalizes the Hamiltonian dynamics of the Painleve'-2 equation to the case with many degrees of freedom, while maintaining the integrability property. The evolution eventually leads to a highly asymmetric state, no matter how weak the symmetry breaking parameter of the Hamiltonian is. This suggests a potential mechanism for strong asymmetry in the production of quasi-particles with nearly identical characteristics. The model's integrability also yields exact exponents for the scaling of the density of the nonadiabatically excited quasi-particles.
item.dc:creator: Bhavay Tyagi, Fumika Suzuki, Vladimir A. Chernyak, Nikolai A. Sinitsyn

item.title: A JT/KPZ correspondence
item.description: arXiv:2511.02529v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We point out a correspondence between the Jackiw--Teitelboim (JT) gravity and the stationary measure of the Kardar--Parisi--Zhang (KPZ) equation on an interval. By relating the Schwarzian limit of the double-scaled SYK to the weakly asymmetric limit of the open ASEP, we establish that the path-integral measure defining the Euclidean evolution between two end-of-the-world branes in JT gravity can be interpreted as the stationary measure of the KPZ equation on an interval with Neumann boundary conditions. We also establish the match between correlation functions.
item.dc:creator: Masataka Watanabe

item.title: Topological subregions in Chern Simons theory and topological string theory
item.description: arXiv:2511.08746v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The standard, gapped entanglement boundary condition in Chern Simons theory breaks the topological invariance of the theory by introducing a complex structure on the entangling surface. This produces an infinite dimensional subregion Hilbert space, a non-trivial modular Hamiltonion, and a UV-divergent entanglement entropy that is a universal feature of local quantum field theories. In this work, we appeal to the combinatorial quantization of Chern Simons theory to define a purely topological notion of a subregion. The subregion operator algebras are spaces of functions on a quantum group. We develop a diagrammatic calculus for the associated $q$-deformed entanglement entropy, which arise from the entanglement of anyonic edge modes. The $q$-deformation regulates the divergences of the QFT, producing a finite entanglement entropy associated to a $q$-tracial state. We explain how these ideas provide an operator algebraic framework for the entanglement entropy computations in topological string theory \cite{Donnelly:2020teo,Jiang:2020cqo, wongtopstring}, where a large- $N$ limit of the $q$-deformed subregion algebra plays a key role in the stringy description of spacetime.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Wong

item.title: Exact general solutions for cosmological scalar field evolution in a vacuum-energy dominated expansion
item.description: arXiv:2601.15226v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We derive exact general solutions (as opposed to attractor particular solutions) for the evolution of a scalar field $\phi$ in a universe dominated by a background fluid with equation of state parameter $w_B = -1$, extending earlier work on exact solutions with $w_B > -1$. Straightfoward exact solutions exist when the evolution is described by a linear differential equation, corresponding to constant, linear, and quadratic potentials. In the nonlinear case, exact solutions are derived for $V = V_0\ln \phi$, $V = V_0 \phi^{1/2}$ and $V = V_0/\phi$, and the logarithmic potential also yields an exact first integral. These complicated parametric solutions are considerably less useful than those derived previously for a universe dominated by a barotropic fluid such as matter or radiation with $w_B > -1$. However, we generalize the slow-roll approximation and show that it applies to all sufficiently flat potentials in the case of a vacuum-dominated expansion, while it never applies when the universe is dominated by a background fluid with $w_B > -1$.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Hu, Robert J. Scherrer

item.title: Spin chains for ADE quiver theories
item.description: arXiv:2602.22065v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The spectral problem of four-dimensional superconformal quiver gauge theories can be mapped to one-dimensional spin chains with restricted Hilbert spaces, where the composition of neighbouring spins follows the path algebra of the quiver. To better understand such spin chains, we compute the one-loop planar dilatation operator for the 4d N=2 ADE quiver gauge theories obtained by orbifolding the N=4 Super-Yang-Mills theory and marginally deforming by independently varying the gauge couplings. This extends previous work which was mainly focused on the Z2 quiver. We characterise the general features of the resulting ADE spin-chain models and construct the 2-magnon Bethe ansatz for holomorphic states. We also evaluate, at large N, the N=2 superconformal index of these gauge theories and use it to study their protected spectrum in specific sectors.
item.dc:creator: Jarryd Bath, Konstantinos Zoubos

item.title: Direct Scattering of the Focusing Nonlinear Schr\"odinger Equation with Step-like Oscillatory Initial Data
item.description: arXiv:2603.02855v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this manuscript we set up the direct and inverse scattering problems for step-like traveling wave solutions of the nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation. Specifically, we consider the initial data $u_0(x)=u_e^\ell(x)$ for $x<0$ and $u_0(x)=u_e^r(x)$ for $x>0$, where $u_e^\ell(x)$ and $u_e^r(x)$ are elliptic traveling wave solutions of NLS. More generally, we consider initial data satisfying $u_0(x)\to u_e^\ell(x)$ as $x\to-\infty$ and $u_0(x)\to u_e^r(x)$ as $x\to+\infty$. Under the assumption that $u_0-u_e^\ell \in L^{1,2}(\mathbb{R}^-)$ and $u_0-u_e^r \in L^{1,2}(\mathbb{R}^+)$, we formulate the direct scattering problem and establish analytic properties of the scattering data. We then formulate the inverse problem as a Riemann--Hilbert problem and prove its solvability, thus proving the existence of the nonlinear Schr\"odinger solution with the above step-like initial data. Finally, we observe that our Riemann--Hilbert formulation is a special case of the one arising for full soliton-gas initial data.
item.dc:creator: Tamara Grava, Robert Jenkins, Xiaofan Zhang, Zechuan Zhang

item.title: Fundamental fields in the deformed $W$-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2604.09471v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a simple Lie algebra. Frenkel and Reshetikhin introduced the deformed $W$-algebra $\mathbf{W}_{qt}(\mathfrak{g})$. In this work, we give a formal version of this definition. In this setting, we reformulate and prove the well-definedness of an algorithm (arxiv:2103.15247, arxiv:2205.08312) inspired by the Frenkel-Mukhin algorithm (arXiv:math/9911112) which, starting from a given dominant monomial $m$ satisfying some degree conditions, produces elements of the deformed $W$-algebra. Then, we apply this algorithm to construct explicitly some specific elements of $\mathbf{W}_{q,t}(\mathfrak{g})$. In particular, we apply this to prove a conjecture of Frenkel and Reshetikhin in arXiv:q-alg/9708006 in types $B_\ell$, $C_\ell$, and for some nodes in other types. This framework opens up new possibilities for studying explicitly fields in the deformed $W$-algebra $\mathbf{W}_{q,t}(\mathfrak{g})$.
item.dc:creator: Hicham Assakaf

item.title: Quantum Fisher Information and Separable Energy Minima in Spin Systems
item.description: arXiv:2605.03022v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a general method to bound the minimum energy of spin Hamiltonians over separable states with fixed single-particle reduced density matrices. The method uses a two-particle optimization and identifies conditions under which the resulting bound is tight. For ferromagnetic Ising and Ising-like interactions on any regular graph, we obtain an exact separable-energy minimum expressed through the quantum Fisher information (QFI) of the local state; a symmetric separable state attains the optimal correlation on every bond. For fully connected ferromagnetic Ising-like systems, ground-state correlations give a lower estimate of this single-particle QFI with a rigorous O(1/N) finite-size error. Further exact results relate symmetric-separable minima of antiferromagnetic Ising-like and XY-like models to local expectation values, and ferromagnetic spin-1/2 Heisenberg chains to quantum fidelity. We also derive bounds for separability across fixed partitions into contiguous blocks.
item.dc:creator: G\'eza T\'oth, J\'ozsef Pitrik

item.title: Cyclic source pairings for Penrose--Sparling non-Hausdorff twistor spaces
item.description: arXiv:2606.04054v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We determine the stable source information carried by the gluing-groupoid algebra of the Penrose--Sparling non-Hausdorff twistor double. Relative normal residues define supported analytic $K$-classes with specified normal orientations. For a smooth double along a closed submanifold, we compute the full geometric periodic cyclic homology as the parity sum of the compactly supported cohomologies of the ambient manifold and the doubled locus. In the physical model, $K_0\cong\Z^4$ and $HP_0\cong\C^4$, with both odd groups zero. Four explicit cocycles give integral $K$-coordinates and exhaust continuous periodic cyclic cohomology; every periodic cyclic pairing on supported source classes is therefore a linear combination of rank and degree. Finite moments recover $K$-valued normal profiles modulo integral common line twists. A first-jet criterion tests mixed-line triviality and identifies the residue with the torsion cokernel of a generically invertible second fundamental form for pullback quotients. The degree-one Euler modification and the diagonal Coulomb embedding have identical filtered $K$-profiles in every algebraic $SL_2$ representation, while their rank-two Ward connections are respectively indecomposable and split. We give the Euler connection and its transition between both root charts. An elementary holonomy realization shows that the inherited ambient and divisor transverse classes annihilate supported source classes. The relative degree pairing uses an additional choice of opposite defect orientations.
item.dc:creator: Ioannis P. Zois

item.title: Rank Recursion for $q$-Whittaker and Macdonald Operators
item.description: arXiv:2606.12796v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we introduce and prove a set of rank recurrence relations for $q$-Whittaker and Macdonald operators. We also derive an explicit expression for the $k$-th power of the $q$-Whittaker operators in terms of the $q$-deformed binomial probability distribution, and we express the rank recurrence relations for the Macdonald operators in terms of the Cauchy determinant.
item.dc:creator: Philippe Di Francesco, Hieu Trung Vu

item.title: Quantum Computing Algebra (QCA), the theory and implementation
item.description: arXiv:2606.17621v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a real geometric algebra framework designed for the direct translation of the Dirac formalism into geometric algebra representations. Unlike previous approaches based on positive-definite signatures, QCA employs a split-signature construction that enables a natural realization of quantum states and operators while simplifying computational implementation. We further present an implementation of QCA using the \textit{GAALOP} software and show how quantum gates and multi-qubit systems can be efficiently represented and generated computationally. As an application, we demonstrate the use of QCA in quantum game theory, where the real-algebraic formulation provides computational advantages for modeling entangled strategies and quantum interactions. The proposed framework establishes a practical bridge between the abstract formalism of quantum computation and efficient geometric algebra implementations.
item.dc:creator: Jaroslav Hrdina, Dietmar Hildenbrand, Oliver Rettig

item.title: Indistinguishability Theory for Identical Particles with Invariant Degrees of Freedom
item.description: arXiv:2609.14428v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Identical particles have dynamically invariant labels in all setups where their degrees of freedom can be partitioned into two parts, which we call internal and visible, with the visible part subject to unitary evolution, while the dynamically invariant internal part accounts for the partial distinguishability of particles. We give the explicit form of the visible state in terms of the indistinguishability function, generalizing the standard symmetrization/antisymmetrization postulate for bosons/fermions with internal modes. The indistinguishability function on the symmetric group accounts for the permutation symmetry of the dynamically invariant label state and gives a self-contained description of the symmetry spectrum of the visible state. It is shown that the indistinguishability of single particles emitted independently from a stable source is completely characterized by the projective measures on the symmetry spectrum. We reveal a hierarchy of successive upper bounds on the projective measure of indistinguishability in terms of marginal projective measures. We point out an experimentally feasible way to get the upper bounds on the indistinguishability of an arbitrarily large number of single photons by direct experimental readout of their marginal projective measures. We also analyze the indistinguishability of coherent superpositions and convex mixtures and resolve a recently posed problem.
item.dc:creator: Valery Shchesnovich

item.title: Velocity Averaging for the Wigner Equation with Electromagnetic Fields
item.description: arXiv:2609.21885v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We discuss the application of $L^2$-based velocity averaging to the Wigner kinetic equation governing the quantum evolution of the Wigner transform of a density operator of a particle subjected to an external electromagnetic field. This extends the $L^2$-based averaging lemma from [F. Golse, J. M\"oller: Commun. Math. Sci. (2026)] to electromagnetic fields. We make use of the magnetic or gauge-invariant Wigner transform due to Stratonovich [Sov. Phys. Dokl., 1:414-418, 1956] which differs from the usual definition by a phase factor involving the circulation of the magnetic vector potential along a line segment. The magnetic Wigner transform obeys the Wigner equation in the generalized phase space variables $(x,v=\xi-A(t,x))$, which is a more natural setting for the application of velocity averaging. Since the magnetic Wigner equation contains a first order derivative in the spatial variable, we obtain compactness in $L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$ but no gain in regularity.
item.dc:creator: Fran\c{c}ois Golse, Jakob M\"oller

item.title: Antipodal Self-Duality for Generalized Fishnets from Integrability
item.description: arXiv:2610.00803v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Antipodal self-duality (ASD) is a remarkable property that relates an amplitude to itself, after performing a suitable kinematic map and reversing the letters of the symbol (more precisely, acting with the antipode of the Hopf algebra of the de Rham analogs of multiple polylogarithms). ASD has been seen in only one process in planar $\mathcal{N}=4$ super-Yang-Mills theory, and its physical origin is unknown, motivating a search for ASD in other contexts. Recently, ASD was found to hold for square fishnet integrals in a strongly-deformed version of planar $\mathcal{N}=4$. In this paper, we investigate the properties of polynomials in ladder integrals under the ASD transformation that leaves the square fishnet invariant. Our basic building blocks are determinants of certain matrices of ladder integrals, that are labeled by partitions or Young diagrams, and automatically obey the Steinmann relations. We employ integrability-based representations of such determinants, which are essentially matrix-model integrals, and the theory of symmetric polynomials to find many more ASD quantities -- linear combinations of determinants whose coefficients are expressed using the combinatorics of partitions. As a byproduct, we provide an alternate proof that square fishnet integrals obey ASD.
item.dc:creator: Lance J. Dixon, Claude Duhr, Francesca C. Fernandes, Victor Mishnyakov

item.title: Plunge bounds for Fourier concentration operators: geometry, smoothing, and wave packets
item.description: arXiv:2610.09406v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove a single-logarithm bound for the eigenvalues in the plunge region of Fourier concentration operators, removing the extra logarithmic factor in the Kulikov--Dam Larsen bound for two general admissible sets throughout each fixed exponential window. For bounded spatial and frequency sets $A,B\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ of positive measure with finite upper codimension-one Minkowski boundary content, the number $\Lambda_\varepsilon(cA,B)$ of eigenvalues in $(\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon)$ satisfies $\Lambda_\varepsilon(cA,B)\le C(d,A,B,\beta)c^{d-1}D(1+\log_+(c/D))$, where $D=\log(1/(\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)))$, for every fixed $\beta>0$, $c\ge2$, $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, and $D\le\beta c$, with $\log_+t=\max(0,\log t)$. The argument uses positive band-limited smoothing and requires no symmetry, convexity, or connectedness. In dimension two, the corresponding exponential-window estimate has a constant uniform in the window parameter. We also determine the optimal coordinate-Lipschitz constant $d-1$ for recursive decompositions of balls and standard simplices in every dimension, and obtain box-frequency estimates with explicit geometric constants. For $C^1$ convex bodies in three dimensions, the optimal infimum of recursive coordinate slopes is $2$. Uniform real-order Bessel estimates give independent disk and ball bounds at every spectral threshold, including an explicit deep-tail term. For smooth strictly convex planar frequency bodies with positive curvature, we prove correlation estimates for aligned Gaussian packets at arbitrary relative scales and quantitative lower bounds on the cost of estimating spatial blocks separately. Together these results connect the global spectral bound with sharp geometric constructions and the cancellation retained by grouping boundary interactions.
item.dc:creator: Ahmadreza Azimifard

item.title: Finite-time quantum equilibration from local correlations
item.description: arXiv:2610.16351v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study equilibration of a fixed subsystem coupled to an initially maximally mixed bath. We show that the worst-input mean-square error, maximised over observation windows of length $T$, is bounded from above and below by the mean square of a complete local autocorrelation on $[0,T]$. The constants depend only on the subsystem dimension, and no assumption on degeneracies of energies or energy gaps is required. Subtracting the stationary part of the correlation gives equilibration to the temporal state; retaining it gives thermalisation to the maximally mixed state. We then obtain explicit bounds for two static Hamiltonian families. A periodic spin-clock model thermalises on $O(n\log n)$ windows at fixed accuracy despite an exponentially small positive energy. A randomly dressed commuting model, with interaction range $O(\log N)$, has expected error $O(N^{-b}+T^{-1})$ while retaining an extensive family of conserved observables. We explain how the locally weighted spectrum determines these bounds.
item.dc:creator: Piotr \'Cwikli\'nski

item.title: Two-scale band geometry and ballistic transport for limit-periodic Schr\"odinger operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.01303v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove strong ballistic transport for one-dimensional Schr\"odinger operators with bounded limit-periodic potentials. If the nested periodic approximants satisfy $\|V-V_n\|_\infty=o(p_{n+1}^{-2}e^{-\eta p_n})$, with $\eta>7\sqrt{2R}$ and $\|V\|_\infty\le R$, then the rescaled Heisenberg position has a nonzero strong limit on a weighted $H^2$ class containing the Schwartz space. In contrast to earlier continuum results requiring exponential accuracy in $p_{n+1}$, the exponential weight here involves only $p_n$; the ratios $p_{n+1}/p_n$ may be unbounded. Folding identifies each ordered large-cell band, away from symmetry momenta, with a fixed translated small-cell band. This confines near-collisions of all bands to a common neighborhood controlled at the smaller period. A period-uniform quadratic-form estimate, ordered-gap summation, and a graph-norm comparison linear in the potential error then give the limiting velocity. Moments of orders $0<r\le4$ have two-sided ballistic growth as a corollary. An explicit example separates the two approximation conditions.
item.dc:creator: Moises Gomez Solis

item.title: Bondi-Sachs formalism on past light cones and an analogue of the integral mass formula
item.description: arXiv:2611.08958v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Following a proposal that the thermodynamic aspects of general relativity can be found in the evolution of the past light cones of arbitrary worldlines, we generalise the Bondi-Sachs formalism to these surfaces. The observer may accelerate and rotate their tetrad, the spacetime may contain matter and a cosmological constant, and no symmetry is assumed. We impose regularity conditions at the vertex of each light cone and along the polar axis, including general axial conditions that allow for shear. Given a suitable prescription for the stresses of matter, the Einstein field equations can then be integrated hierarchically from data on a single light cone, and the regularity at the vertex fixes all constants of integration. The solution reveals a universal property: to first order in the observer's proper time, the evolution of the metric and of the four-momentum crossing the light cones is independent of the specific behaviour of matter. As an application, we derive, for an observer immersed in matter, an analogue of the integral mass formula of black hole mechanics.
item.dc:creator: Matheus G. Barbosa

item.title: Local Quantum Metrology: Precision Limits for Observers in QFT
item.description: arXiv:2611.17948v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: How precisely can an observer estimate a parameter related to a quantum field? This question is answered for quantum-mechanical systems using the SLD--Bures--Fisher metric and the quantum Cram\'er--Rao bound. However, local algebras in relativistic quantum field theory are of type III: they carry no trace, so that states are not described by density matrices in the algebra, and they have no pure normal states, such that the SLD quantum Fisher information and the quantum Cram\'er--Rao bound cannot be defined in the usual way. We define the SLD (Bures) quantum Fisher information on arbitrary von Neumann algebras through Uhlmann's transition probability and prove a quantum Cram\'er--Rao bound for collective measurements. We also show that the bound is sharp, and equals the largest classical Fisher information obtainable by measurements in the region.
item.dc:creator: Markus Fr\"ob, Albert Much

item.title: Localization identities for spectral determinants: two-dimensional QCD and Ising field theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.21724v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Spectral determinants encode the meson spectra of planar two-dimensional QCD and of Ising field theory in the two-particle Bethe-Salpeter approximation. We derive localization identities for these determinants which express their logarithmic derivatives with respect to the spectral parameter in terms of Baxter $Q-$functions evaluated at special points, proving previously conjectured relations. Our derivation uses finite-rank commutation relations and virial identities of the underlying integral spectral operators. We identify a sufficient rational closure condition on the symbol of these operators that extends localization to a broader class of spectral problems and determines the evaluation points. Applications include generalized two-dimensional QCD with a quartic gauge-field potential and symbols interpolating between the QCD and Ising cases. We also give a general construction of the spectral operators and establish conditions for the finite-rank reduction on which localization relies.
item.dc:creator: Bercel Boldis, Nikolay Gromov, Gregory P. Korchemsky, Alessandro Testa

item.title: FLZ integrability in the 't Hooft model
item.description: arXiv:2611.21787v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the 't Hooft equation describing mesons in large-$N_c$ two-dimensional QCD with arbitrary unequal quark masses. Using its Fredholm formulation and the associated Baxter finite-difference equation, we investigate the relations between spectral determinants and canonical Baxter $Q$-functions. We derive special-point identities for the Baxter solutions by exploiting finite-rank commutator relations of the underlying integral operators. We also determine the spectral residues of the inhomogeneous solutions and obtain exact expressions for eigenfunction normalization factors in terms of values at distinguished complex points. These results establish the unit-residue property of the Baxter expressions entering the Fateev-Lukyanov-Zamolodchikov (FLZ) spectral-determinant identities. As a further application, we prove the nondegeneracy of the meson spectrum for arbitrary unequal quark masses. We further identify a broader class of integral operators exhibiting the same mechanism, which we refer to as FLZ integrability, and illustrate its applicability to the meson spectral problem in Ising field theory. Our approach reveals a connection between the analytic structure of Baxter equations and the theory of completely integrable Fredholm operators.

item.title: Well-posedness and finite-time breakdown for Euler-alignment systems with diffusive chemotaxis
item.description: arXiv:2611.27940v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate a recent class of pressureless Euler systems arising in biological contexts, in which the velocity evolution is driven, besides the nonlocal alignment interaction, by the gradient of a concentration self-produced by the population. We first establish local existence and uniqueness of strong solutions, in a class requiring no spatial derivative of the initial population density, together with a continuation criterion. We then derive sufficient conditions on the initial data for finite-time breakdown in the multidimensional setting, with an explicit upper bound for the maximal time of existence. Numerical simulations complement the analysis and illustrate the transition between regular and singular regimes, and the role of the chemotactic strength in the onset of blow-up.

item.title: Interface Invariants of Rhombohedral Graphene with Layer-dependent Potentials and Couplings
item.description: arXiv:2611.29093v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Domain walls in the perpendicular bias of rhombohedral (ABC-stacked) graphene bind valley-resolved interface modes whose signed number is fixed by a bulk-difference invariant. We determine which values of this invariant are reachable when the layer potentials are arbitrary monotone profiles, as produced by screening, and when the interlayer couplings vary from bond to bond. Within the single-particle continuum model, the invariant of an $m$-layer stack equals the difference of occupied angular weights of the zero-momentum levels, which reduces the classification to the ordering of those levels. At equal coupling, nonlinear monotone potentials reproduce exactly the set of invariants of linear potentials, also under the requirement of a common energy gap: screening moves phase boundaries but creates no new invariant values. With bond-dependent coupling, we characterize all occupied configurations. The range of attainable invariants is unchanged, but the gaps inside it are filled, beginning at five layers. Reflection-symmetric stacks realize a large subfamily with a guaranteed common gap, and lower bounds on single-bulk gaps complete the set of invariants with a common global gap for five and six layers. Among the examples is an eight-layer domain wall defined purely by gates, whose number of co-propagating channels per valley switches from 8 to 16 as the gate strength increases. Exact transfer-matrix calculations of the interface spectrum reproduce every predicted signed crossing count. A norm bound gives the minimum spread of interlayer coupling compatible with a prescribed gap.

item.title: Two-loop correction to the complex-bion amplitude in a quasi-exactly solvable sextic oscillator
item.description: arXiv:2611.29701v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this study, a quasi-exactly solvable sextic potential is analyzed by two diagrammatic calculations. At positive coupling, factorization fixes the ground-state energy $E_0$ exactly and forces every perturbative coefficient to vanish. Using only Feynman diagrams, we verify this cancellation explicitly through third order. After continuation to negative coupling, the formal zero mode becomes nonnormalizable. A real instanton remains, but its one-instanton contribution to \(E_0\) vanishes. In particular, the leading shift in energy arises from a complex neutral bion. Taking an exact constrained family, we calculate its local median amplitude through two loops. The direct diagrammatic sum gives $c_{\rm 2L}^{\rm diag}=-0.750000(5)$, in excellent agreement with the exact-WKB value $-3/4$.
